webTest.title: Web Test (model)
webTest.subtitle: One click randomizes your strong demo classes, searches the web for leaf photos, and runs your live MobileNet pin — table fills one row at a time with GT, prediction, model, and latency.
webTest.poolHint: {count} classes (pepper bacterial spot, corn rust, potato blight, tomato early blight, squash mildew, grape/apple/raspberry healthy, and more).
webTest.cropHintHint: Same idea as Check a crop: if the model’s crop disagrees with the GT crop (e.g. grape→soybean), mark Crop mismatch instead of Yes.
webTest.found: Classifying {count} web images against your live model…
webTest.scorelineBand: Yes {correct} · Abstain {abstain} · No {wrong} / {n} ({pct}% yes overall; {answered}% of answered). Abstain = score < {thr}% or model not_sure.
webTest.gtNote: GT is the intended search class for that row (from your reviewed high-likelihood set), not a human-verified label. Model + ms badges come from the live HF classifier response.
webTest.empty: Click run to randomize classes and fill this table.
webTest.waitingRows: Waiting for the first classified image…

localTest.title: Local Test (real-world)
localTest.subtitle: Same table as Web Test, but samples random photos from model/data/real_world_set (PlantDoc-mapped labels). Quality gate + leaf crop + confidence band against your live MobileNet pin.
localTest.poolHint: 50 labelled field/web leaves under model/data/real_world_set. Each run picks N at random (optionally tune or final split only).
localTest.missingImages: labels.csv has {csv} rows but no image files were found under {dir}. Images are often git-ignored — unzip/copy the set locally, or mount it in Docker.
localTest.gtNote: GT is the PlantVillage label from labels.csv (mapped from PlantDoc). Still not a pathologist re-check, but far more reliable than a DuckDuckGo search target.
localTest.empty: Click run to sample the local set and fill this table.

guidelines.title: Photo guidelines
guidelines.intro: Follow these quick checks so the model can detect visible symptoms more reliably.
guidelines.focusBody: Hold the camera steady and let the leaf fill most of the frame.
guidelines.lightBody: Avoid harsh shadows and bright glare on the leaf surface.
guidelines.wetBody: Water drops can hide spots and reduce diagnosis quality.
guidelines.oneBody: JPEG, PNG, or WebP up to 25 MB. Large phone photos are shrunk automatically.

results.subQuality: The quality gate stopped before the disease model. Retake so the leaf is clear.
results.subUnsure: The model saw the leaf but the score is too low to name a disease.
results.subOk: Understand the signs. Start with safer, practical care.
results.translationUnavailable: Telugu guidance is unavailable right now, so this result stays in English.
results.footer: Demo capstone — photos stay in your browser only. Confirm important decisions with a local agricultural expert.

guide.title: Growing guide
guide.intro: Practical habits for healthier crops. This demo guide supports the CropCare AI capstone — not a substitute for regional agronomy advice.
guide.tip1Body: Use daylight, hold steady, and fill the frame with the affected leaf.
guide.tip2Body: Many fungal issues start on older foliage before spreading upward.
guide.tip3Body: Match symptoms over a few days and ask your local extension office before costly treatment.
guide.tip4Body: Remove heavily infected plant material and avoid working in wet fields to limit spread.
